palette.name: Wada 209: Ivory Buff, Yellow Orange, Salvia Blue
palette.label: Wada No.

groups.made_with: ChatGPT project; attempt 1 with instructions v3, attempt 2 believed to be v4; attached the palette strip

attempts.asked: "Using the instructions, please create an appropriate room that showcases this color palette"
attempts.note: v3's corrections held: white ceiling, no lit built-ins, no token objects, calm detail, a believable breakfast room. But it is basic and uninspiring, and the colour is still assigned object by object: walls buff, bench orange, chairs and curtains blue. The gaps between a strong orange and a muted blue are not bridged. Measured, the walls read tan and the blues grey (difference 11-13 on lit areas); the orange is closest. The patterned cushions and blue-and-white jug are the only places the colours meet. Hydrangeas again.

attempts.asked: "Using the instructions... Please create a room using this color palette"
attempts.note: Owner: "much better", but not something to stop scrolling for. Brighter and more resolved: steel-framed arched windows, a striped bench cushion that finally bridges the orange and blue, light oak and stone foundation, white-ish ceiling. Still: blue chairs and blue cabinets (one colour per category), blue hydrangeas and a landscape painting again, and no clear memorable move. The line after the image does not name an idea, which v4 asks for: check that v4 is the version pasted in the project.

attempts.asked: Same chat as attempt 2: a detailed follow-up written by the studio, with an explicit keep list and six numbered changes (morning sun; diagonal ivory and salvia checkerboard floor; striped chairs "at the ends of the table"; deeper greyer cabinets; blossom in an ochre jug with a napkin; a botanical print in a walnut frame).
attempts.note: It made all six changes and kept the room, camera, table, pendant and bench: a detailed follow-up with a keep list held. Owner: more worthy of sharing, but an overcorrection. The striped chairs landed on the two nearest chairs because the studio's wording ("the ends of the table") was ambiguous; with the floor, bench and chairs all patterned it is now busy. The square recess around the arched window was already in attempt 2 and was kept as asked. Measured, the ceiling is actually whiter than before and the walls no warmer; the orange creep is the sunlight itself, which is golden rather than clear.

attempts.asked: Same chat: four changes with a keep list (all chairs in salvia linen with yellow-orange piping; the back wall's recess follows the window's arch; clear, pale morning sun; a statement opal-glass pendant with a 1930s feeling and matching wall lights).
attempts.note: Chairs, back wall and light all fixed as asked; the owner finds it decent. The new pendant tries too hard and does not suit the room: it is a reworked version of the old dome, built to the studio's own detailed description. The blue cabinets repeat the chairs and their colour has drifted deeper and greyer, which the studio's previous follow-up asked for. The cabinets add little.

attempts.asked: Same chat: remove the pendant and wall lights and let it choose a fresh pendant for the room; replace the blue cabinets with one freestanding antique walnut sideboard.
attempts.note: The fresh pendant is calmer and more believable, and the walnut sideboard adds a dark anchor. But after four follow-ups the room has drifted: it feels crowded, the bench sits off-centre from the window and wall, the sideboard is not needed (less is more for a palette image), and the colours are wandering (the blues read brighter and bluer than the greyed Salvia Blue). The owner asks for an occasional reset: re-attach the palette, restate the light, and settle everything naturally without overcorrecting.

palette.name: Studio 10: Mexico City (Casa Pink, Volcanic Black, Marigold, Jacaranda)
palette.label: Studio No.

groups.made_with: ChatGPT project with instructions v2; attached the site's palette strip (which labels the colours Field, Weight, Accent, Bridge)

attempts.asked: "Using the instructions... Please create a high-quality image of a room with this color palette" (no "luxurious")
attempts.note: Strong colour commitment and a calmer ceiling than the salon; all four colours clearly present; 9:16. But the ceiling is painted the same pink as the walls, as in every room so far; the styling is token (a purple vase and a purple box placed to tick the colour off); a large abstract wall sculpture reads as a model room, not a home. Owner: it should feel lived-in and luxurious but approachable, a room a social-media audience can imagine as their own.

palette.name: Wada 213: Vinaceous Cinnamon, Apricot Yellow, Pale King's Blue
palette.label: Wada No.

groups.made_with: ChatGPT project with the owner's instructions v1 and Wada's colors.json; commands "#213" and "card #213"

attempts.note: The owner's favourite so far: coffered and lit ceiling, panelled pale walls, a peach velvet sofa, two yellow chairs, each colour repeated at several scales (cushions, vase, rug), symmetrical and calm. Exactly 9:16. Measured, the palette is muted and warmed: the sky blue walls read grey-blue (difference 10-16), the lemon yellow reads golden-mustard (17), the peach sofa darker. Stock elements again: landscape painting under a picture light, tiered drum chandelier, olive tree, cream throw.
A gold-foil, letterpress-style paper card, one swatch per colour with its name. Close to the real values: blue within 0.8, peach and yellow about 5 (visibly a little warmer). Exactly 9:16.

palette.name: Wada 254: Corinthian Pink, Sulpher Yellow, Olive, Laelia Pink
palette.label: Wada No.

groups.made_with: ChatGPT project with the owner's instructions v1 and Wada's colors.json; command "#254"

attempts.note: Bold and on-palette: pink walls match almost exactly (difference 1.6-2.1); olive velvet headboard and bench, pale yellow quilt, pink throw. But the olive goes golden and the yellow peachy (about 7-8), it reads glossy and rendered rather than photographed, and it is 3:4, not 9:16. Stock elements: crystal drum chandelier, cove glow, landscape painting under a picture light, candles.

attempts.asked: Instructions v2. Attached the palette strip and asked: "Using the instructions, can you create a luxurious room that utilizes this color palette?"
attempts.note: Big step up in realism and composition: a music salon with tall windows, a real fireplace, a plaster relief instead of a landscape painting, a sculptural pendant, exactly 9:16. But the ceiling is over-ornamented, and the palette is zoned rather than designed: pink on the left (sofa, chaise, curtains), olive on the right (chairs, bookcase), with token crossovers (one olive cushion, pink books) that read as box-ticking. Measured, the colours drift warm and dusty: pinks go dusty rose (difference 11-17), the pale yellow walls go tan-cream (11), so the 4000 K line did not fully hold. Beige marble floor and stone dilute the palette.

groups.made_with: ChatGPT, from two phone screenshots of the trio page (the new measured card and the colour list) and the full v0.5 prompt

attempts.asked: The two screenshots plus the trio page's v0.5 prompt, pasted in full.
attempts.note: The placement is right: sage panelling, a rose velvet channel-tufted bed, ivory bedding and boucle bench, brass, dark floor, centred and straight on. But it is bland, and measured off-colour: the golden light turns the sage walls olive-khaki (hue 41 degrees too warm, twice the strength; difference 15-18) and the ivory beige (14-22); the whole image carries a strong yellow cast. Massive arched library built-ins in a bedroom because the house style lists them. Stock props: hydrangeas, landscape painting, candles, trailing plant.

attempts.asked: Same chat: "Make it look more luxurious."
attempts.note: Generic luxury tropes take over: crystal tiered chandelier, cove lighting, tufted bench, candle on a gold tray. The room darkens and the walls go brown-olive (difference 23-29 from sage); the ivory bedding turns tan. Reads as an obvious AI image. Stored from a screenshot of the chat, so slightly lower quality.

groups.made_with: ChatGPT, from a screenshot of the palette card

attempts.asked: First short prompt: photorealistic room from this palette, soft ambient lighting.
attempts.note: Everything in the dark half of the palette; the pale field colour is missing. Amber light browns the mustard and the steel.

attempts.asked: Revision: lilac walls, keep the plum sofa, mulberry rug.
attempts.note: Walls fixed, but a purple sofa on a purple rug. The mustard ended up on a chair, not the throw the palette asks for.

attempts.asked: New chat: item-by-item placement plan with a contrast rule.
attempts.note: Over-corrected: grey sofa, pale rug, the palette reduced to a few pieces. Light too white and neutral.

attempts.asked: General prompt: the palette card is the brief, use your own judgment.
attempts.note: The palette commits again and the pale rug separates the sofa. Light flat and clinical.
A warm filter over the whole image: salmon walls, over-processed, the cove glow looks forced.

attempts.asked: Shorter prompt: light as a moment, colours true, never filtered.
attempts.note: Competent but generic: a tight crop of furniture, stock styling, no architecture.

attempts.asked: Same chat, one line: more luxury and intentional, as if designed by an expert; try other room types.
attempts.note: A bedroom. Real architecture, one focal point, the palette used with intention, natural light. Still some stock styling.

attempts.asked: Same chat: asked it to review its own work (in the owner's own general words, not the scorecard).
attempts.note: Back to a living room, but with architecture: arched window, arched built-in bookcases, beamed ceiling, fireplace as the focal point. Pale walls, deep plum built-ins, plum seating on a pale rug, one mustard throw. Natural low sun and lamps. Still candles; the sun patch leans golden.

groups.made_with: ChatGPT, from a screenshot of the palette card

attempts.asked: Planning prompt: read the palette, choose a room and one bold idea, describe a 9/10 for each category (including Materials), then create the image.
attempts.note: Box-ticking. The card listed walnut as a material and named the dark colour "Walnut Shadow", so walnut became architecture: a whole walnut bookcase plus a walnut table (another attempt made a wall of walnut planks). A designer would have used it for one table. Leather, jute and boucle added on top: every category shown off, nothing designed.
